articles.title: Alarm in Denmark after Russian ship fires at military helicopter
articles.body:
A Russian ship fired flares at a Danish military helicopter off the southern coast of Denmark on Monday, triggering alarm in Copenhagen as the Kremlin's belligerence against Europe ramps up.
"The Russian frigate fired two flares at the helicopter. One of the flares fired passed within a short distance of the helicopter," the Danish armed forces announced late Monday night.
European nations have accused Moscow of conducting a campaign of so-called hybrid warfare to destabilize the continent while it also persists in its full-scale invasion of Ukraine — but capitals and NATO have hesitated about an escalatory response to Russia.
"With an increasingly aggressive and assertive Russia, that has intensified the hybrid war against Europe. And that tests and challenges NATO. Russia wants to intimidate and sow discord. Our response is to stand closer together and strengthen the defense of Denmark and Europe," she added.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen linked the incident in Denmark to the incursion of a drone into Lithuania's airspace overnight. The drone was shot down by NATO fighter pilots and was likely coming from neighboring Belarus, Lithuanian authorities said.
"These are not isolated incidents. They are part of a broader pattern of Russian aggression and provocation against Europe, testing our readiness and our resolve. Russia will find our resolve only growing stronger," von der Leyen wrote on social media.
"This is another reckless Russian action meant to intimidate Allies. But Russia is not succeeding. We continue to safeguard our territory and we continue to support Ukraine," NATO spokesperson Allison Hart said.
Denmark will drag in the Russian ambassador to explain the crew's actions, a senior official in Copenhagen announced Tuesday morning.
"The armed forces report that one of the air force's helicopters was fired upon with so-called flares in connection with routine photographic coverage of a Russian frigate in the waters off Gedser. This is completely unacceptable. Therefore, Russia's ambassador has been summoned for a conversation about the incident," said Lars Løkke Rasmussen, Denmark's foreign minister.
This article was updated with comments from Ursula von der Leyen and NATO spokesperson Allison Hart.

articles.title: U.S. Air Force AGM-190A missile goes from design to combat fast
articles.body:
- Air Force Special Operations Command said its AGM-190A Havoc Spear cruise missile passed a spring 2026 combat evaluation conducted with U.S. Africa Command.
- AFSOC and U.S. Special Operations Command developed the low-cost, modular missile through a cooperative research and development agreement in under three years.
The U.S. Air Force’s Havoc Spear cruise missile has passed a combat evaluation and is now cleared for broader use across special operations and conventional aircraft, Air Force Special Operations Command announced. The missile, officially designated the AGM-190A, was tested in a live operational setting during the spring of 2026.
AFSOC ran the evaluation in partnership with U.S. Africa Command, launching the missile from a C-130 aircraft in what the command described as a test configuration. Officials said the missile performed accurately and met AFSOC’s requirements for a small cruise missile, clearing the way for wider fielding.
Havoc Spear is built to be modular and mission-adaptable, meaning operators can configure it for different targets or effects, and the design is intended to keep production costs and timelines down compared with older cruise missile programs. AFSOC first revealed the missile’s name publicly in May 2026 at the Special Operations Forces Week conference in Tampa, Florida, where officials described it as capable of delivering long-range precision strikes with both kinetic and non-kinetic effects.
“Havoc Spear’s range and capabilities expands standoff options, giving commanders a versatile tool to neutralize threats without putting platforms or personnel in immediate danger,” said U.S. Air Force Lt. Gen. Mike Conley, AFSOC commander.
“It’s also not lost on us the value of being able to test a new weapon system in combat, and prove its success on the battlefield early on in the process,” Conley said.
The decision to run the evaluation through AFRICOM ties the missile’s early record to one of the U.S. military’s more active counterterrorism theaters. AFRICOM has spent years targeting militant networks across the continent, and Gen. Dagvin Anderson, the command’s chief, framed the test as part of that ongoing mission.
“We work every day to disrupt the networks that have made Africa the epicenter of global terrorism,” said U.S. Air Force Gen. Dagvin Anderson, AFRICOM commander.
“These successful operational assessments prove we will continue to bring the unique capabilities only the U.S. can provide in order to defend U.S. interests alongside our partners,” Anderson said.
Havoc Spear’s development path skipped much of the traditional acquisition process. U.S. Special Operations Command led the effort on AFSOC’s behalf, using a cooperative research and development agreement, or CRADA, with an industry partner rather than a standard program of record. That approach allowed the missile to move from design through combat testing in under three years, compared with the five to seven years such programs typically take.
“To outpace our adversaries, we can’t rely on traditional acquisition pipelines,” said U.S. Air Force Col. Robert Johnston, AFSOC director of strategic plans, programs and requirements.
“AFSOC is eager to explore more agile, lesser-known pathways to modernization to deepen industry partnerships, leverage calculated risks, and rapidly deliver capabilities to our warfighters,” Johnston said.
AFSOC has not disclosed the missile’s cost, its production rate, or which aircraft beyond the C-130 used in the AFRICOM evaluation will carry Havoc Spear as it moves toward wider use.

articles.title: Turkey calls on Iran, US to stop attacks in Gulf region, says strikes harm peace efforts
articles.body:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Tuesday that reciprocal attacks in the Gulf were impacting peace efforts to end the US-Iran war and called for them to immediately stop, adding that Ankara also valued the stability of its neighbor Iran.
Speaking at a joint press conference with his Azerbaijani counterpart in Baku, Fidan also said freedom of passage should be allowed in the Strait of Hormuz, and the pre-war status quo should be reinstated, adding that Ankara was in touch with all involved parties to find a solution to the matter.
This comes as Iran claimed that an oil tanker exploded and caught fire after colliding with mines in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM denied the report that a collision caused the explosion, instead stating that the ship had actually been struck by an Iranian missile last month and had recently been struck again by an Iranian drone
"The IRGC's false claim is yet another example of their lies and intimidation attempts while they try to impede commercial vessels in the strait," CENTCOM wrote in a post on X/Twitter.
CENTCOM says Iranian drones strike Panama-flagged oil tanker
According to Iranian state media Fars, the tanker was identified as the El Gaia, a ship flying under the Panamanian flag. The ship was later ferried to shore in Oman.
Additionally, Iranian-backed Houthis have been disrupting shipping lanes with attacks in the Red Sea and have been striking Saudi cities and assets.
On Friday, Fidan discussed regional developments and recent attacks targeting Saudi Arabia in a call with his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill two people, including a child, medics say
articles.body:
Israeli strikes in Gaza kill two people, including a child, medics say
CAIRO/GAZA, Sept 15 - Israeli airstrikes hit a vehicle, killing at least two Palestinians, including a child, and wounding seven others in the northern Gaza Strip neighbourhood of Sheikh Radwan on Tuesday, the territory's health officials said.
The Israeli military said it had struck a militant in the area, without elaborating.
Witnesses said some of the casualties resulted from a second strike that hit near a group of people who rushed to help in the rescue. A video, that wasn't immediately verified by Reuters, showed a missile exploding near at least five men.
Palestinians earlier held funerals in Gaza for two people who were killed by Israeli strikes a day ago, Ahmed Al-Batsh and
Rafat Zummar.
Batsh was a local Hamas commander, according to Hamas sources and the Israeli military. Medics said Batsh died in an attack on his vehicle in northern Gaza Strip.
The Israeli military said in separate statements that it had killed both men, and it described Zummar also as a Hamas commander. Hamas didn't immediately comment on Zummar's affiliation.
Relatives and friends paid farewell to Batsh's body draped in a white shroud and a Hamas green flag inside Gaza City's Al Shifa Hospital. An M16 assault rifle was placed on top of the body.
"Israel thinks... it will eliminate the resistance and the spirit of jihad (devotion) within us," said Khalil Al-Batsh, a relative of the dead Hamas militant, of the killing.
"I tell them that this cowardly operation only strengthens our people's determination to continue on this path,” he told Reuters at the funeral.
An October 2025, U.S.-backed, ceasefire halted large-scale fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended Israeli strikes and there has been little progress on steps towards permanent peace.
Hamas accuses Israel of violating the ceasefire and undermining efforts to implement U.S. President Donald Trump's broader plan to end the Gaza conflict, which includes the Israeli withdrawal from the strip and the disarmament of Hamas.
Israel says Hamas has been violating the deal.
More than 1,300 Palestinians, mostly civilians, have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect, according to the territory's health officials, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed.
Hamas does not usually disclose information about fatalities among its fighters. REUTERS

articles.title: Russian drones killed a man and injured eight in Kyiv, hitting two gas stations
articles.body:
Russian drones killed one man and injured eight people in Kyiv on the morning of 15 September, hitting two gas stations along with warehouses, a restaurant, and an office building, the National Police reported. The strikes came in a night-long wave of 200 drones that also hit Odesa Oblast in southern Ukraine.
What Russia hit in Kyiv
The first drone came down at a gas station in the Darnytskyi district shortly after 06:00, and more drones hit warehouses in the Obolonskyi district around the same time, the Kyiv Military Administration said. The strike critically wounded a man who was standing near the Darnytskyi station.
The attack resumed after 08:00. A drone struck a non-residential building in the Solomianskyi district, then a second gas station in the Holosiivskyi district, where heavy smoke rose over the site. Mayor Vitalii Klitschko reported the number of injured climbing through the morning, from two to four to eight, with two of them in serious condition. Emergency services put six of the eight in the Solomianskyi district, which took a second hit around 10:00.
The man hurt at the Darnytskyi station died in hospital at about 10:35. Beyond the two stations, police recorded damage to warehouses, a fast-food restaurant, and a business center.
The wave that carried them
Russia launched 200 strike drones from 18:00 on 14 September, the Air Force said: Shahed types including jet-powered ones, Gerberas, and Parodiya decoys, flown from Russia and occupied areas. Air defense downed or suppressed 187 of them by 08:00, with hits recorded at seven locations and debris falling at three more. The attack was still running when that count was published.
Russian forces hit Odesa Oblast at the same time. Russian forces struck residential buildings, logistics sites, and port and transport infrastructure, oblast head Oleh Kiper said, damaging roofs, facades, and windows of private houses along with dozens of garages and cars.
The same night, NATO fighters shot down a drone over Lithuania that had crossed from Belarus, and Ukrainian forces struck the Syzran refinery in Samara Oblast and a warehouse in Taganrog.
Why gas stations
Kyiv's filling stations have been under systematic attack since 10 September, when a drone came down at a station near a shopping mall. On 11 September, jet drones hit two Ukrnafta complexes on opposite banks of the city and returned to strike one of them a second time.
Unlike filling stations in the border oblasts, which Russia hits with cheap short-range drones, the Kyiv stations are being struck with its most expensive ones. Ukrainian stations are mostly struck with the Geran-4 Seeker, the variant fitted with machine-vision targeting, according military observer Oleksandr Kovalenko of Information Resistance.
More than 300 gas stations have been attacked across Ukraine since the current wave began, according to energy ministry data. The strikes have moved gradually from front-line oblasts deeper into the country, and about 80% of damaged stations return to work.

articles.title: Zelenskyy: Russia hits Ukraine's energy system, we retaliate
articles.body:
Zelenskyy: Russia hits Ukraine's energy system, we retaliate
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has stressed that Russia continues to attack Ukraine's energy facilities, while the defence forces continue to respond with strikes on enterprises that support the aggressor state's defence industry.
Source: Zelenskyy on X (Twitter)
Quote: "Russia continues to attack our energy sector, regular logistics and critical infrastructure. And our responses to them for this are tangible.
There are new results from the defence forces of Ukraine regarding the refinery in Syzran. There was also a strike in Taganrog on a drone production facility, as well as on a drone preparation and launch site in Oryol Oblast. Targets were hit in the Black Sea as well.
I thank every one of our warriors for the effectiveness of our long-range sanctions!"
Background:
- On 14 September, US President Donald Trump said that Ukraine and Russia had supposedly agreed not to strike energy facilities.
- Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy commented in his evening address on 14 September on the US proposal for a mutual halt to strikes on critical infrastructure. "If this can become the first step towards de-escalation – a step involving an end to Russian strikes on our critical infrastructure and our strikes in response – then Ukraine is ready to support de-escalation," he said.
- The Financial Times, citing sources familiar with the matter, reported that talks on halting strikes on energy facilities have been under way for some time, but Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin does not want to reach an agreement before winter sets in.

articles.title: AFSOC Launches Developmental Cruise Missile in Combat in Africa
articles.body:
NATIONAL HARBOR, Md.—Air Force Special Operations Command recently fired small cruise missiles from an AC-130J gunship during combat operations in Africa, verifying the developmental weapon’s safety and accuracy.
The combat test validates that the missile, the AGM-190A Havoc Spear, is ready for “broader real-world use,” AFSOC said in a Sept. 14 announcement.
Havoc Spear, built by Leidos and originally nicknamed “Black Arrow,” is a 200-pound class weapon with a range of 400-plus nautical miles.
In a roundtable with reporters before the announcement, AFSOC officials said they fired two AGM-190s this spring at two validated ground targets in the U.S. Africa Command area of responsibility. No further details about the targets were revealed, but AFSOC said the evaluations proved the missile is “accurate, reliable, and operationally ready.”
“Havoc Spear gives commanders the essential standoff capability to neutralize threats without putting our personnel and platforms in immediate danger, and it’s also proving its tactical value on the battlefield,” said Col. Robert Johnston, director of strategic plans, programs, and requirements at AFSOC.
Havoc Spear is among several low-cost cruise missiles developed by industry in recent years in response to the Pentagon’s demand for greater combat mass.
Developed by Leidos, the system dates back to 2021 and the company’s experience with the GBU-69 Small Glide Munition. The company signed a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement in 2022 with U.S. Special Operations Command and AFSOC to further develop the missile, leading up to the combat evaluation four years later.
Now the Pentagon is moving to expand that work. In July, SOCOM awarded Leidos a $27.2 million contract for 45 missiles, putting the average cost of Havoc Spear at around $600,000 per unit. But AFSOC officials noted that total is for low-rate initial production, with the cost expected to drop as much as two-thirds as production ramps up.
The cost, however, will depend on the scale of production, and AFSOC officials are hoping to use Havoc Spear not only across the command, but the entire Air Force.
“Our ultimate goal is to try to get this on every type of SOF platform, as well as conventional platform possible, in multiple launch modes,” said Johnson.
The weapon can be fired via launch tubes off the ramp of the AC-130, but it can also be mounted on pylons or palletized to be dropped from cargo aircraft. Its payload can even be modular, opening up a additional options.
AFSOC officials said they mostly plan to use the initial batch of missiles from the July contract for more testing. The first of those missiles is expected to arrive next fall, officials said.
“We’re still doing further development on other platforms and other launch mechanisms, and so we’ll use that initial tranche to try to get after more development than employment,” said Johnson.
Which special ops aircraft comes next isn’t clear—Johnson said it “really depends on what’s available.”
“To be quite honest, with current operations, we have to piecemeal what assets we can actually employ and get test dates on,” he said.
In the long term, AFSOC is thinking big—Johnson suggested Havoc Spear could one day be incorporated into the Air Force’s Family of Affordable Mass Missiles program.
FAMM is a major Air Force-wide effort to mass produce more affordable, less exquisite air-to-ground missiles. In July, the Pentagon announced framework agreements for multiyear production of Anduril’s Barracuda; CoAspire’s Rapidly Adaptable Affordable Cruise Missile, or RAACM; and Zone 5 Technologies’ AGM-188 Rusty Dagger—the service could get a total of 8,000 missiles annually once production ramps up, and budget projections show plans to acquire up to 28,000 over the next five years.

articles.title: Zelenskyy appoints Konstantyn Humeniuk as Commander of Ukraine’s Medical Forces
articles.body:
Zelenskyy appoints Konstantyn Humeniuk as Commander of Ukraine’s Medical Forces
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has signed a decree appointing Konstantyn Humeniuk as Commander of the Medical Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Source: decree on the President's Office website
Quote: "Humeniuk Konstantyn Vitaliiovych shall be appointed as Commander of the Medical Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine."
Details: In a previous decree, the president dismissed Anatolii Kazmirchuk from this position.
For reference: Konstantyn Humeniuk is a colonel in the medical service and an educator, and holds the academic degrees of Candidate of Medical Sciences and Doctor of Medical Sciences. He holds is an Honoured Doctor of Ukraine and is a recipient of the Borys Paton National Prize of Ukraine.
In May 2014, he served in the ATO The ATO or Anti-Terrorist Operation is a term used from 2014 to 2018 by the media, the government of Ukraine and the OSCE to identify combat actions in parts of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts against Russian military forces and pro-Russian separatists. It was later renamed the Joint Forces Operation . In 2017, he became Chief Surgeon of the ATO, and from 2018 to 2019, he served as Chief Surgeon of the Joint Forces Operation. He has held the post of Chief Surgeon of the Armed Forces of Ukraine since 2019.
In May 2022, at a military mobile hospital in a frontline town near Bakhmut, he performed Ukraine's first advanced laparoscopic operation to remove a kidney on a patient suffering severe gunshot damage to the organ.
Background:
- Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapatyi submitted a proposal to dismiss incumbent Medical Forces Commander Anatolii Kazmirchuk on 4 August.
- Anatolii Kazmirchuk holds the rank of major general of the medical service. He is a military physician, Doctor of Medical Sciences and professor. He was appointed Commander of the Medical Forces on 19 November 2023 by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
- In 2024, Anton Shevchuk – head of the medical service of the 82nd Separate Air Assault Brigade, who in July 2023 discovered Chinese-made tourniquets in his brigade and requested that the Medical Forces Command replace them – was reassigned to a lower position in another unit following a formal reprimand from his superiors.
